Running in three steps
You host it. Here is everything that means.

Updating takes one command
./queryglow update backs up first, checks the nginx config it manages before anything restarts, keeps the running image, builds the new one, and checks that the new version is actually serving. Who builds QueryGlow
I'm Max, a solo developer from Germany. I built QueryGlow because I wanted my databases in a browser tab wherever I work, without a desktop app on every machine and without another subscription. I answer every email myself, usually within a day. You get the full source code, so your install never depends on me being around.


How it started
“I want Supabase-grade UI, but I DON'T want all the underlying tooling. Literally just the UI so I can inspect my DBs and do queries. […] This doesn't exist? Who's gonna create it? I'd pay for this on a lifetime deal.”Simon Høiberg on X, November 2025

“You feel that they really care about their clients and the quality of their product.”Jean-Francois, Mildor Violon, verified customer





Questions before you buy
Short answers, with links to the details.
pgAdmin, DBeaver and Adminer are free. Why pay $79?If a free tool does the job, keep it. QueryGlow is for when you want one web GUI that your whole team opens from a URL on a server you run, and you would rather pay once than per seat. The live demo shows you the interface before you decide. Details: pgAdmin vs QueryGlow, DBeaver vs QueryGlow and phpMyAdmin alternatives.

What do I need to run it?A Linux server with Docker (512 MB RAM minimum, 1 GB recommended), a domain pointing at it for HTTPS, and a non-root user with sudo. Clone the repository and run ./queryglow install: it sets up the HTTPS certificate, the login for your team and the app on a fresh server, or plugs into the nginx you already run. The setup guide walks through each step.

What happens at checkout?Checkout runs on Stripe and asks for your email, your GitHub username and a billing address; a business tax ID is optional. You pay by card, PayPal or Amazon Pay, and Stripe shows the final amount including any tax before you pay. The repository invite goes to your GitHub username and usually arrives within minutes. You also accept the terms, which include giving up the withdrawal right because access is immediate.

Can I get a refund?No. You get the full source code the moment you pay, and that cannot be taken back. That is why the live demo exists: the real app on a sample database, read-only, AI switched off, no signup. Take your time with it, and email [email protected] if a question is still open before you buy.

How do updates work?Every 1.x update is included. On your server, ./queryglow update backs up QueryGlow's own settings and data (not the databases it connects to), checks the nginx config it manages, builds the new release and checks that it is serving; if it is not, it rolls back to the previous release on its own. ./queryglow update --check only tells you whether a new release exists, and the app itself never checks for updates. A 2.x release may be a new purchase, as the license says. See what shipped so far in the changelog.

Can my whole team use it?Yes. Your whole team uses the same install from one URL, behind one shared login (Basic Auth at the web server, asked once per browser). There are no per-user accounts and no roles, so everyone with the login has the same access. One license covers every server you run.

Does the AI see my data?No. Ask AI sends your database type, table and column names with their types, and your prompt. Never rows. It uses your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, entered in the app (stored encrypted on your server) or set in .env, and the SQL it writes waits in the editor until you click Run. Ask AI is optional, and it is switched off in the public demo.

Is it secure enough for production?Safe Mode, in the Query Editor and for agents, always blocks DROP DATABASE and server file or command execution. By default it also blocks DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, dropping indexes, views, sequences and schemas, and DELETE or UPDATE without WHERE; setting QUERYGLOW_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true on the server lifts that tier. On a connection marked production, the Query Editor shows the statement and asks before any write (on by default; can be turned off in Preferences). Saved passwords, SSH keys and AI keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, SSH host keys are pinned on first use, and the app runs behind nginx with HTTPS and Basic Auth, as the security docs explain.

Which databases are supported?Six: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, CockroachDB and TimescaleDB. Connections to all of them sit side by side in one install. SQL Server and Oracle are not supported.

Can I use it for client work?Yes. Run QueryGlow on your own infrastructure and use it for client projects, on every server you run. A client who wants their own installation needs their own license, and the source code is not passed on to clients. The details are in the license.

Is it open source?No. QueryGlow is sold under a commercial license with the full source code included. The GitHub repository is private, and buyers get read access to it, so you can read the code, patch it and build it yourself. Redistributing it is not allowed.

Can I pay with PayPal or Bitcoin?PayPal, yes: pick it on the Stripe checkout page, next to card and Amazon Pay. For Bitcoin, email [email protected] and you get the payment details by reply. After payment, send your GitHub username; the repository invite is sent by hand, so allow a few hours.
